# yantrad

> The Yantra control-plane daemon. Every client talks to this and nothing else; no client ever talks
> directly to a managed machine. An axum server with a read-only JSON API over a background
> snapshot, the writes (`POST /heartbeat`, `new`, and `edit`/`up`/`down`/`resume` per workspace), a
> WebSocket that bridges a workspace's session to a browser, and the dashboard itself. It is an HTTP surface over
> `yantra-core`, not a second copy of the logic.

## Source

- [src/main.rs](src/main.rs): resolves its bind addresses from Tailscale, fails closed, serves `/healthz`, shuts down on SIGTERM. Plain HTTP on 7717; TLS is `tailscale serve`'s (`just https`, port 8443) and never this crate's; `GET /api/about` names that origin as `https`, and the dashboard, not the daemon, moves a browser there (Y-652). It also listens on `$RUNTIME_DIRECTORY/yantrad.sock` (`/run/yantra` by default), where `tailscale serve` proxies to; a missing directory is a warning and TCP alone (ADR-0042). The set it binds is what `write.rs`'s authoriser refuses over TCP, so it is passed to the router rather than re-derived. The tree itself is composed in `app`, apart from `serve`, so a test can drive it without binding a port (Y-169).
- [src/refresh.rs](src/refresh.rs): one background task per data class, writing `yantra_core::snapshot::Snapshot`. The interval is a constant, low enough to keep the ssh masters warm. No request path touches ssh. The agents task also feeds the notifier, once its reading is already in the model, and a successful `up`, `down` or `resume` wakes it at once (Y-639). Two more tasks run [watch.rs](src/watch.rs): the PR poll every `PULLS` (120 s), and discovery on the `ATTENTION` clock. `settle` is where a readiness sweep lands: it keeps each report, keeps them all on a failed sweep, and drops a name neither the sweep nor the tailnet holds (Y-579). **Readiness is a class on this sweep rather than a handler that runs `doctor`** (Y-168): it is the dearest look of the five, and a browser polling it per request is the ssh storm this module exists to prevent. It runs at the same interval as the rest because Q6 left nothing to tune and because the agents sweep already runs `claude` on every machine that often — **not** because a slower loop would pay a handshake, which it would not: the other four sweeps hold the `ControlPersist=300` masters open regardless. It takes `write::term()`, since nobody is sitting at this terminal either (I-36). **The attention class is the one that leaves the tailnet, and the only one on an interval of its own** (Y-172): GitHub is a network call, so the rule keeping ssh off the request path binds it for the same reason, but here a faster poll is pure cost — it warms no master and spends the owner's own GitHub quota, which their `gh` and `git push` draw on too. Five minutes, against a measured `X-Poll-Interval: 60` from `/notifications`, which `EVERY` would have polled at twice the rate GitHub asks for. The `Forge` is passed in like the `Inventory`, so the loop is drivable from a fake. **The grant check and the repository list are two more classes on that same clock** (Y-175, Y-342): both read GitHub with the grant the daemon holds, and all three wake early when the grant is set or cleared, so a sign-in shows its repositories now rather than at the next tick. An unreachable GitHub is read again after 5 s, doubling up to the normal interval, and an answer of any kind waits the full interval (Y-731). One failed read keeps the last good inbox, repository list, hidden organisations and grant check, marked with the failure; the second failed read in a row replaces the reading, and a grant that is gone or refused replaces it at once (Y-745). **The proxy's admin API is a class of its own on the fleet's interval** (Y-777): while the daemon trusts a proxy account, `look_at_proxy_admin` connects to `127.0.0.1:2019` with a 2 s limit and gives the answer to `doctor::proxy_admin`. The journal has a warning each time the port is found open. `spawn` takes whether a proxy account is trusted.
- [src/notify.rs](src/notify.rs): when the diff runs (Y-146). A difference between two consecutive agent readings and nothing more — no poll, no ssh, no timer of its own; [`yantra_core::notify`](../yantra-core/src/notify.rs) decides what a difference *means*. The relay is told the phase's fixed headline as `Title` and, for a failed run, a fixed string in place of the verdict (Y-451); the event log keeps the verdict. **The first look after a start says nothing** and **a failed send drops that notification** — no queue, no retry, no replay, with `yantra-agent`'s `Log` as the precedent for saying the first failure and swallowing the rest. A look that failed notifies nobody, because an unknown fleet is not a changed one. The pass has a budget well under the refresh interval, so a relay that accepts and never answers cannot push the next look out. **The relay comes from `YANTRA_NTFY_URL` and `YANTRA_NTFY_TOKEN`** (Y-147), read once in `main.rs`: an absent URL is a daemon with no relay and not a refusal to start, the token is read from the environment and nowhere else, and the startup line says which of the two it got because a unit's environment is not the shell's. **The relay is now settable** ([ADR-0021](../../docs/adr/0021-the-relay-is-written-to-an-environment-file.md), Y-199): `/settings` and `yantra relay` write the file the unit reads, so the read path here is unchanged and a new relay reaches this daemon at its next start. **And nothing is pushed while a tab is open** (D3 §13): `Viewers` is one timestamp in memory beside the snapshot, the beacon writes it, and a look taken while somebody is watching still runs its diff and drops what it produced — so closing the tab delivers no backlog. A restart forgets it, which is correct.
- [src/api.rs](src/api.rs): `GET /api/{machines,workspaces,sessions}`, read-only. Every answer says whether the look succeeded, failed or has not happened, and how old it is. An `ok` answer carries `retrying`, the failure of the newest look, when the daemon kept a GitHub reading through one failed read (Y-745). **A `workspaces` entry says whether the file loaded** (Y-141) — one that did not is in the list under its name with its reason, rather than turning the whole class into `looked: "failed"`. `machines` also carries each machine's latest heartbeat and its age, joined on the node id; `null` there is *never heard from* and is not a beat that reports zero. DTOs live here rather than as `Serialize` on core's types (ADR-0005) — **`doctor`'s own types are the exception**, because its check names and three states are the JSON contract [D2 §3.1](../../docs/design/02-setup.md) already publishes. **`GET /api/readiness` and `GET /api/machines/{name}/readiness`** (Y-168) serve that sweep, and answer the one check the library cannot: `heartbeat` is *present* with its age where a beat from an agent at this daemon's version or later has arrived, *absent* where none has since this daemon started, *absent* with both versions and the pinned `install.sh` command where the agent is older or sends no version (Y-713; a Mac under a nightly daemon is held to the stable release that nightly builds on), and *unknown* where the tailnet list holds no node of that name — the beats are keyed on the node id (I-5) and a report names a machine the way a workspace does (ADR-0009). The sweep also asks each online tailnet peer that `runsSessions` would count, so a Windows, shared or tagged peer gets no check, and both routes read `Snapshot::checks`, the latest report per machine with its own `age_seconds`, so a poll cannot turn a result into `never` (Y-579). The one-machine route is a **404** for a machine no check has reached. **A path under `/api` that no route claims is a JSON 404 here** (Y-169): the nest carries a fallback of its own, because without one the miss reaches the dashboard's SPA fallback and answers `200 text/html` (I-64). **`GET /api/attention`** (Y-173) serves the GitHub reading in the same envelope and blocks on nothing: reviews and issues as two lists under their own names, unread as a count, and no grant as `looked: "failed"` carrying `yantra github login` — never an empty inbox, which is R-23's unplugged sensor reading zero. It is in [contract.gen.ts](../../web/src/contract.gen.ts) since Y-322, which Y-173 deferred until a file in `web/src` read the route — the entry and the type that checks it belong in one change, and splitting them cost two rows. **`GET /api/readiness/github`** (Y-175, Y-342) is the readiness answer about *this* host — whether the grant the daemon holds is present and still accepted ([ADR-0023](../../docs/adr/0023-the-github-grant-lives-beside-the-relay.md)). A route rather than a tenth check on every report, because an answer about this machine drawn on every machine's card claims something no ssh session asked; and it has no `failed`, since the check carries a look it could not take as *unknown*. **`GET /api/github` and `GET /api/repos`** (Y-342, ADR-0023) are the grant as the daemon holds it — `connected`, the login, the profile image URL, the scopes, whether a sign-in is pending, `expiring` when the last one ended because GitHub issued a token that expires (Y-695), and never the token — and every repository it can see, swept every 300 s and filtered in the browser; no grant is `looked: "failed"` naming `yantra github login`. `GET /api/repos/hidden` (Y-629) names each organisation that owns none of those repositories, on the same sweep, and fails with the list when the list failed. **Three more reads since Y-343**: `GET /api/about` is the build (version, target, date — from [yantra-core's `about.rs`](../yantra-core/src/about.rs)), the uptime, the bound addresses, the tailnet read off the node holding one of them, whether this process holds a relay (`relay`, a bool and never the URL or token, Y-388), and `published` (Y-367, [ADR-0027](../../docs/adr/0027-the-appliance-pulls-its-own-update.md) §2): the newest release's version and whether it is `newer`, in the three-state envelope, read hourly on the sweep and never on the request path. `update` (Y-612) is how far `yantra-update.service` has got, read from `/run/yantra-update` on each request: `null`, a `step` with the bytes received while it downloads, or `failed` with the unit's last stderr lines. The body has no envelope of its own because the other facts are not looks, but `published` is one — a read that failed is `failed` with its reason and never *current*; `GET /api/ssh-identity` is the public half of the daemon's key with its fingerprint and `owner_line`, the `authorized_keys` line for an owner terminal with `from=` set to `listening_on`'s addresses (Y-701), **a 404 before `yantra ssh-identity` has run** because a GET reads and never generates; `GET /api/notifications` is [ADR-0025](../../docs/adr/0025-the-daemon-remembers-what-it-pushed.md)'s ring, newest first, at `age_seconds: 0`. `Machine.address` is the first Tailscale IPv4, `Machine.hub` is the node holding a bound address — the same match `about` makes for the tailnet (Y-582) — and `Session.created_at` is the epoch beside tmux's own string. **`GET /api/readiness/proxy`** (Y-777) is the second answer about this host: *absent* when Caddy's admin API answers on `127.0.0.1:2019` while the daemon trusts a proxy account. No dashboard screen reads it yet.
- [src/watch.rs](src/watch.rs): the PR watch (Y-494, [ADR-0034](../../docs/adr/0034-the-coding-loop-writes-to-github.md) decision 3). `Pulls` on `Fleet` maps `(owner, repo, number)` to a `Tracked`, in memory. `poll` reads each PR with four conditional reads (the pull, its checks, its reviews and its line comments) every `refresh::PULLS` (120 s), and the pure `look` decides: the first look at a PR the start-up rebuild found is a baseline and says nothing, and a PR added later says its first look; a check failed and checks passed are said once per head sha; a review is said when its id is new, it is not `PENDING` and the PR's author did not write it. Merged, closed or `FAILURES` (8) failed looks in a row drop the entry. `discover` adds the open PRs of every workspace's threads on the `ATTENTION` clock and removes nothing, which is also the rebuild at start; `track` adds the PR `pr open` answered. Each entry keeps the last fresh checks (with each output's title and a summary cut at 4 KiB), reviews with their bodies and line comments, which a 304 keeps and a new head drops the checks of; **`GET /api/pulls`** (Y-512) serves them for the Chat's Checks and Fix with agent (Y-495) from memory, with no GitHub or ssh call. The text is `github::Unlogged`, whose `Debug` prints only a length, so no log line carries it (Q5).
- [src/events.rs](src/events.rs): [ADR-0025](../../docs/adr/0025-the-daemon-remembers-what-it-pushed.md), Y-343 — a `VecDeque` of the last 50 events the daemon would have pushed, in `Fleet` beside the beats, and nothing on disk: a restart empties it, which the page says rather than hides (I-59). Filled by `notify.rs` **before** the send, so a dropped send and a daemon with no relay both still remember; by the machines sweep in `refresh.rs` when a machine's `online` goes true to false (`unreachable`); and by `POST /api/relay` before its test message (`relay-test`). A verdict's kind is spelled as `AgentState` spells it. GitHub items are not events, so the titles still never land here. Read and unread are the browser's.
- [src/web.rs](src/web.rs): serves the built dashboard from `YANTRA_WEB`, with a fallback to `index.html` so deep links reach the app. Refuses at startup if that directory holds no `index.html`, and answers a 404 that says how to set it when nothing is configured. **A directory that vanishes after that check answers `503` and logs it**: the startup refusal looks once, and a `YANTRA_WEB` pointing into a deleted git worktree left `ServeDir` answering an empty 404 — the deep link's own status — with nothing in the journal. The check is on the 404 path, which the SPA fallback makes rare while the directory is there; the line is said once and again when it comes back (`yantra-agent`'s `Log`), and the daemon does not exit, because the API, the heartbeat and the terminal socket are all still serving. **The default build embeds nothing** (R-24): a build that wants `web/dist` unconditionally puts npm on every `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` and musl job.
- [src/web/embedded.rs](src/web/embedded.rs): the same dashboard compiled into the binary, so M7's appliance is one file to copy (Y-140). Behind the `embed-dashboard` feature, which is **absent from `default`** — the module is `#[cfg]`'d and `include_dir` is optional, so a default build neither reads `web/dist` nor compiles the macro that would. A `web/dist` with no `index.html` is a *build* error here, which is the directory half's startup refusal moved as early as it can go. It sends an `ETag` and `Vary` on everything, `immutable` on `assets/` and `no-cache` on the rest, and answers a matching `If-None-Match` with `304` (Y-372). **`YANTRA_WEB` wins over it and a set-but-wrong one still refuses**: the embedded copy is fixed at build time and cannot be mistyped, the variable is typed by a person, so the fallible half keeps the refusal rather than being papered over (R-23). Nothing in `just check` or `just ci` may turn the feature on and `--all-features` may appear nowhere; `just no-node` is that omission made into a red build, and [`.github/workflows/embed.yml`](../../.github/workflows/embed.yml) is the one job that builds with it, kept out of `ci.yml` because `ci.yml` has no path filter.
- [src/write.rs](src/write.rs): `POST /api/workspaces`, `PATCH /api/workspaces/{name}` and `POST /api/workspaces/{name}/{up,down,resume}` — the CLI's own verbs and nothing more (`yantra new`, `edit`, `up`, `down`, `resume`), bar `GET /api/here` and `POST /api/viewing`, which a terminal cannot mean. **`POST /api/relay` is `yantra relay`** ([ADR-0021](../../docs/adr/0021-the-relay-is-written-to-an-environment-file.md), Y-199): it writes `/etc/yantra/daemon.env`, then sends a test message to what it wrote, so a **502** means the relay is on disk and the message did not arrive. Nothing reads it back — no route serves the URL or the token. **`GET /api/here`** (Y-589) answers `{machine}`: the tailnet machine the request came from, found in the last tailnet look by the caller's tailnet node id from `whois` and not by address (I-5, I-52), authorised like every route (403 for a caller that is not this owner's); `null` for a node the look does not hold, **503** when there is no look or it failed (R-23). **`POST /api/viewing` is the dashboard saying it is open** (D3 §13), authorised like every other write because it stops this daemon pushing to somebody's phone. Authorised per ADR-0016: the caller's source address is resolved **live** via `whois`, and a node that is not this owner's, or carries tags, is refused 403. A `tailscale` that cannot answer is **503**, never 403 — nothing was decided about the caller. **Which address is resolved depends on the door** ([ADR-0042](../../docs/adr/0042-the-proxy-hop-is-proved-by-the-kernel.md), Y-680): on TCP the peer, and never `X-Forwarded-For`; a peer that is one of this daemon's own bind addresses is **403** naming the socket. On the socket `SO_PEERCRED` names the account: root, and the one account `YANTRA_PROXY_ACCOUNT` names (Y-727), is the `serve` hop, whose `X-Forwarded-For` must be one address that is not this machine's (absent or this machine is **403**, a list is **503**); the daemon's own account or a `yantra` group member is this machine; any other account is **403**, except that `GET /join` and `POST /api/join` let it join itself. The verbs that reach a machine await ssh, which the read path may not; `new` touches no machine and answers **409** for a name already taken, returning the created workspace in the body because the read model will not hold it for up to 30 s. `edit` (Y-126) rewrites only the fields the body names — `"startup": null` clears the command, an absent key leaves it, and a body naming nothing is a **400** — and answers the workspace as it now reads, in the same shape `new` answers. It reaches the machine **only** when `machine` really changes, and then refuses rather than strands: a tmux session still open on the machine being left is a **409** (I-30, and `yantra down` clears it), and a machine that could not be asked is a **503** rather than a move (R-23). The refusal is [`edit.rs`](../yantra-core/src/edit.rs)'s; this route only carries it. **`up`, `down` and `resume` map every variant they can refuse with, exhaustively and with no wildcard** (Y-135): **409** where the world already answers and a person changes that answer — an agent holding at claude's trust dialog (I-49), one whose credential the gate did not find (I-44), a session opened as a shell, a workspace that runs something of its own, a `repo` the machine does not have, and a macOS machine with no tmux server and no one logged in at its screen, so no LaunchAgent can start one ([ADR-0018](../../docs/adr/0018-the-tmux-server-carries-the-macos-login-session.md) §1, Y-151, Y-632); **503** where nothing was decided — ssh, tmux, terminfo, a status that could not be read, a `resume` whose two sources disagree (R-23); **500** only for this daemon's own — no state directory, a session id it could not generate. Before this everything but a workspace error fell through to 500, and the dashboard drew a state the daemon had named correctly as *the verb ran and failed*. **`GET` and `POST /api/workspaces/{name}/repair` are the one write this daemon does not compose** ([ADR-0020](../../docs/adr/0020-a-raw-write-only-from-broken-to-valid.md), Y-190): `yantra repair` on the wire, feeding `/w/{name}/repair`. Two refusals bound it — **409** for a file that already loads, since a workspace that works is changed field by field, and **400** for bytes that still will not, carrying the next error rather than a summary, because the caller is answering the one it was shown. `from_repair` is a mapper of its own for that second reason: in `from_workspace` a `Malformed` or a `Blank` is this daemon reading its own files and so a 500, and here it is the bytes the caller sent. **The `GET` lives here rather than in `api.rs`** and is on the same authoriser: a file's raw bytes are the one thing `GET /api/workspaces` does not publish, and it answers the same 409, so opening it is itself the question *is this broken*. **`POST /api/machines/{machine}/clone` is `yantra clone`** (Y-344): `{url, path}` is checked in [clone.rs](../yantra-core/src/clone.rs) before any machine is asked — `https://`, `ssh://` or `user@host:path` with no credential in it, and a destination that is absolute or `~/…`, never climbs and holds no shell character, each refusal a **400** — and then `git clone --progress` starts inside a tmux session named `clone-<slug>` and the route answers **202** `{machine, session}` at once. Nothing awaits the clone: progress is that session's terminal socket (ADR-0022), completion is the probe, and asking twice attaches (I-30). No token goes with it (ADR-0023 §4). A macOS machine with no tmux server is `up`'s **409**. **`dirs` takes `make` beside `path`** since the same row: one directory name, checked as one segment (**400** otherwise), made with `mkdir -p` under a parent that must already be there (**409** otherwise), and then the same listing. **`POST /api/github/login` and `DELETE /api/github` are `yantra github login` and `logout`** (Y-342, [ADR-0023](../../docs/adr/0023-the-github-grant-lives-beside-the-relay.md)): the first answers the code to type at github.com and polls in a task of its own, so the grant is live the moment the flow completes and is written beside the relay for the next start; the second removes the line and clears the grant. One flow at a time — a second `POST` while one waits is a **409** — and no client id is a **500** naming `YANTRA_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`. **`POST /api/join` and `GET /join` are the join command** (Y-387, [ADR-0029](../../docs/adr/0029-a-machine-joins-itself.md)): the body is `{user}` and nothing else, the machine is named from the caller through `whois` and the tailnet list, so a machine joins only itself, and a config that already names it is kept. `GET /join` sits outside `/api`, serves the script as plain text, and makes the key on first use. **`POST /api/join/forget-host-key` is `yantra forget-host-key`** for the caller, named the same way (Y-621): the script calls it after it turns Tailscale SSH off, because sshd answers with another host key. The podman proof is [tests/join.rs](tests/join.rs). **`POST /api/machines/{machine}/install` is `yantra install`** (Y-386, [ADR-0028](../../docs/adr/0028-yantra-installs-the-bare-minimum-on-a-machine.md)): it answers **202** at once and runs the install in a task the daemon owns. Yantra stops waiting after 15 minutes and says the install may still be running there, because only the local `ssh` stops (I-27). The result is an `installed` or `install_stopped` event in the ring, whose `commands` carries each command left for a person verbatim, and then the readiness sweep runs early. A second `POST` for a machine whose install still runs is a **409**. A name outside the ssh-destination rule (dot-separated labels of letters, digits and `-`, none starting with `-`, at most 253 characters) is a **400**, and nothing is spawned. **`POST /api/update` is `yantra update`** ([ADR-0027](../../docs/adr/0027-the-appliance-pulls-its-own-update.md) §3, Y-368): it creates the empty file `/home/yantra/yantra-update.requested` and answers **202** with no body. `yantra-update.path` starts the root unit, which installs the current release and restarts this process. The daemon fetches nothing. A box with no `/usr/local/bin/yantra-update` is a **409** naming `install.sh`. **`POST /api/workspaces/{name}/threads/{thread}/{message,commit,push}` are `yantra commit --draft`, `commit` and `push`** (Y-492, [ADR-0034](../../docs/adr/0034-the-coding-loop-writes-to-github.md)): the machine commits with its own identity and a message `claude -p` writes there, and pushes with its own credential. `message` answers `{message}`, `commit` takes `{message?}` and answers `{commit, subject}`, `push` answers `{remote, branch}` and never a URL. An empty message is **400**; no thread is **404**; a turn or revert in the thread, no identity, nothing to commit, no `origin`, a refused push and a Mac with no tmux server are **409**; `claude` failing is **502**; ssh and tmux are **503**; five minutes on the machine is **504**; other git failures are **500**. No message, diff or refusal text is logged. **`POST /api/workspaces/{name}/mentions`** (Y-562) is what the Chat composer offers after `@` and `$`: `{harness, thread?}` answers `{files, truncated, skills}` from one script in the thread's worktree, or the workspace's repository before a thread opens ([mention.rs](../yantra-core/src/mention.rs)). An unknown harness is **400**, a directory that is not a repository and an unknown thread are **409**, and ssh is **503**. **`POST /api/workspaces/{name}/commands`** (Y-563) is what it offers after `/`: the same body answers `{commands}`, Claude's slash commands from one bounded `claude -p` ([command.rs](../yantra-core/src/command.rs)), and `[]` at once for an ACP harness, whose list comes on the chat socket. No claude there is **409**, and the rest map as `mentions` does. **`POST /api/workspaces/{name}/threads/{thread}/pr` is `yantra pr open`** (Y-449, ADR-0034 decisions 1 and 3): it takes `{title?, body?}`, each defaulting to the tip commit's, and answers `{number, url, created}`; `created` is `false` for a PR already open, which is read before the tip and again after a `422` "already exists", so a retry or a race never duplicates one (§B4). It uses the daemon's grant and a running turn does not refuse it. **409**: no grant, no upstream, a remote off github.com, a branch ahead of, behind or diverged from its upstream, no title anywhere, a repository the grant cannot see (GitHub's 404), and any other GitHub 422. **`POST /api/workspaces/{name}/threads/{thread}/merge` is `yantra pr merge`** (Y-496): it takes `{number}`, the PR the owner confirmed, squash-merges it with the daemon's grant at the head the daemon reads, deletes the remote branch, and answers `{number, url, branchDeleted}`. A running turn does not refuse it. **409**: no grant, no open PR, another PR than the one confirmed, a PR already merged, one GitHub will not merge (405) and a head that moved between the daemon's read and its merge (409), each with GitHub's words. The dialog shows the PR number and no commits, so the web pins the number and not the head; `yantra pr merge` pins both. **`DELETE /api/workspaces/{name}/threads/{thread}` is `yantra chat rm`** (Y-496), the Chat's Remove worktree: a running turn or revert is **409**, then `thread::remove` kills the keeper and removes the worktree, branch, checkpoints, journals and images, and it answers **204**. The keeper's reader ends with its pane, so the chat registry lets the thread go. Only the workspace and thread id are logged. **`POST …/threads/{thread}/terminal` is `yantra chat terminal`** (Y-498): it opens or attaches the thread's tmux session in its worktree and answers `{machine, session}`, the address of the session socket. A running turn does not refuse it, because the Chat says the shell and the agent share the tree. 404 is no thread, 409 a Mac with no tmux server, 503 a machine or a tmux that failed.
- [src/chat.rs](src/chat.rs): `GET /api/workspaces/{name}/chat?thread=<id>&after=<cursor>`, the chat on a WebSocket ([ADR-0026](../../docs/adr/0026-the-chat-is-a-stream-json-bridge-in-the-daemon.md), Y-356). It calls `allowed()` before the upgrade. The first turn picks the thread's harness: Claude over `claude -p`, or Codex, Gemini, Grok or opencode over ACP (Y-434), and a refused login is a `notLoggedIn` failure with the command to run. A Claude thread is a [`claude::Session`](../yantra-core/src/claude.rs) in the thread's own worktree; any other harness is one [`acp::Agent`](../yantra-core/src/acp.rs). **A turn outlives its socket, its ssh pipe and the daemon** ([ADR-0035](../../docs/adr/0035-a-chat-turn-outlives-its-ssh-pipe.md), Y-447): each agent runs in a [keeper](../yantra-core/src/keep.rs) on its machine, and `Registry`, in `Fleet::chats`, holds one task per live keeper that reads it, reconnects when ssh drops, answers what the mode answers and keeps the checkpoint. A socket subscribes and owns nothing, so a close detaches; only `cancel` or the thread's removal stops a turn, and a cancelled turn still running after 10 s is killed. Each event carries a `cursor`, `<run>:<line end>:<part>`; `?after=` sends only the events after it, and `thread.started` carries the cursor it continues from, or none for a whole replay. `refresh.rs` adopts the keepers a restart left. A request nobody is attached to see sends one Y-451 notification. A Claude keeper holds its `claude` across turns ([ADR-0041](../../docs/adr/0041-a-claude-keeper-holds-the-thread.md), Y-658): a turn Claude opens when a background task ends is the next turn, with its checkpoint and diff and, with no tab attached, one `Phase::Completed` notification; it closes after 30 minutes with no turn and no task, a task pins it until 4 hours pass with no line from Claude, and it is replaced between turns past half the output cap unless a task runs. An ACP keeper stays for the next turn, and stops after 15 minutes with no turn or past half the output cap; an agent still running 10 s after its stdin closed is killed. With no thread the first turn opens one and sends `thread.started`; with one, it is found through `thread::list` and replayed: Claude's transcript as deltas, or ACP's `session/load`. Browser frames: `turn`, `answer{requestId, decision, answers?}` (`answers` maps each question text to the labels chosen, for Claude's `AskUserQuestion`; Y-654), `cancel` (which leaves background tasks running), `stopTask{taskId}`, `stopAll`, `revert`, `diff`, `ping` (answered `{"type":"pong"}`; the daemon also sends protocol pings and ends a socket after two misses, Y-668). A `turn` carries the thread's `mode` (Y-453), Supervised when absent: a request the mode accepts is answered by the daemon and never relayed, and on a Claude thread Auto and Auto-accept edits start Claude in its own `--permission-mode`, so the daemon accepts nothing and an edit outside the worktree still opens a card. A `turn` may carry `interaction: "plan"` (Y-565), on a Claude thread only: Claude runs in its own plan mode, the turn runs as Supervised whatever its mode, `ExitPlanMode` is denied without a card, and any other harness gets `badFrame`; a queued turn takes the last one's, and a room wake is never a plan turn. Daemon frames: `ThreadEvent`s, `thread.background.updated{tasks}` among them, `{"type":"queue","threadId","texts"}` and `{"type":"error","kind","said"}` with kinds `unknownThread`, `busy`, `badFrame`, `unreachable`, `notLoggedIn`, which adds `harness`, `machine` and `command`, `checkpoint`, `diff`, and `stopTask`. Each turn ends in a [checkpoint](../yantra-core/src/checkpoint.rs) (Y-448): checkpoint 0 before the first turn, then one per turn's end and a `turn.diff.updated{turn, unifiedDiff, truncated}`; `revert{turn}` restores the files and answers `thread.reverted{turn}`, and is `busy` while a turn starts, runs, keeps its checkpoint or waits in the queue. `diff` answers one `branchDiff{threadId, base, files, filesTruncated, unifiedDiff, truncated}` (Y-490): the whole branch, committed and uncommitted, against the newest commit it shares with its start or `HEAD`. It runs beside the socket's loop, so a turn's events and a `cancel` still flow; a revert in the thread makes it `busy`, and a failure is `diff` (Y-543). A binary frame is an image (Y-424), up to 16 MiB: it lands in the thread's keeper directory through [`image::Images`](../yantra-core/src/image.rs), and gets one reply in order, `{"type":"attached","path"}` or `{"type":"notAttached","kind":"notAnImage"|"unreachable","said"}`. Every Claude keeper gets `--add-dir` on that directory from its start, and `thread::remove` deletes it. One turn at a time in a thread, across every tab and every restart: a second `turn` is queued (Y-561), every socket gets `queue`, an attach gets it even when empty, and the turn's end sends the queue as one prompt to the same agent; a prompt sent during a wake turn waits for its `result`; `cancel` empties it, and a socket follows its thread's next keeper. Each Claude turn gets `--mcp-config` for `/api/mcp` with its `X-Yantra-Thread`, and a room message wakes an idle Claude thread (Y-534, see `room.rs`). `Registry::activity` answers from memory whether a held thread runs a turn and the tool its last `item.started` named, for room presence, and `Registry::changed` is a `watch` that a change of either bumps (Y-551). `GET /api/machines/{machine}/chat` is the session-addressed form, a home thread ([ADR-0046](../../docs/adr/0046-the-owner-types-sudo-in-an-owner-terminal.md), Y-699): `chat::Home` runs Claude in the joined account's `$HOME` with no worktree and no checkpoint, the store holds the thread, and its keeper is `yantra-keep-yantra-home-<id>`. No CLI verb for a turn; `yantra chat new` and `chat ls` open and list threads (Y-488), and `chat new --home` starts a home thread through the daemon. The lifecycle is logged and the content never is.
- [src/passkey.rs](src/passkey.rs): [ADR-0044](../../docs/adr/0044-a-write-needs-the-owners-passkey.md), Y-687. `~/.config/yantra/passkeys.toml` (`0600`) holds each passkey's public key and each session's SHA-256 token hash, never a token. A code (8 characters, 10 minutes, once, five wrong in a row void every open code) enrols a device; a sign-in sets `__Host-yantra_session` for 30 days. Routes: `GET /api/passkey`, `POST /api/passkey/code`, `DELETE /api/passkey/{name}`, `POST /api/passkey/{register,login}/{start,finish}`, `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}`, `POST /api/sessions/revoke-others`, `POST /api/join/code`. A revoke closes the session's open sockets. `write::gate` runs over the whole `/api` nest: no cookie is **401**, a write from a foreign `Origin` is **403**, a Chat turn's `Bearer` agent token reaches only `write::agent_may`, and `write::unchecked` lists what answers signed out. `YANTRA_ORIGIN` in `/etc/yantra/daemon.env` replaces the MagicDNS origin with one the owner names, and changing it costs every passkey (`write::dashboard_origin`). The podman proof is [tests/passkey.rs](tests/passkey.rs).
- [src/tasks.rs](src/tasks.rs): `/api/tasks`, the work the main agent delegates through `yantra mcp` ([ADR-0033](../../docs/adr/0033-other-harnesses-speak-acp-and-claude-delegates.md) decisions 4 and 5, Y-435). `POST /api/tasks` `{machine, harness, repo, prompt}` makes a git worktree on the machine, starts the ACP agent in it ([delegate.rs](../yantra-core/src/delegate.rs)) and answers **201** `{id, machine, harness, repo, worktree, branch}`. `GET /api/tasks` lists them with their state; `GET /api/tasks/{id}` adds the last message and the diff summary; `POST /api/tasks/{id}/steer` `{prompt}` cancels a running turn and sends the prompt as the next turn in the same session, or queues it behind a turn not yet begun, and answers the task (Y-454); `GET /api/tasks/{id}/wait?timeoutMs=N` waits for the task to end and its summary to land, 60 s by default and 600 s at most, and answers the task with `waitTimedOut`; `POST /api/tasks/{id}/stop` cancels the turn and keeps the worktree; `DELETE /api/tasks/{id}` removes the worktree and the branch. A harness other than codex, gemini, grok or opencode, a machine outside the ssh-destination rule, a repo that is not `/…` or `~/…` and a repo that is not a git work tree are **400**; an empty steer and a bad `timeoutMs` are **400**; an unknown id is **404**; a git that refused and a steer to an ended or stopping task are **409**; ssh is **503**. Every route is on `write.rs`'s authoriser. **The `GET`s read memory**, because the main agent polls them: a task takes its summary when its turn ends and again on `stop`, and the wait awaits that in memory. The tasks are in memory, so a restart forgets them.
- [src/mcp.rs](src/mcp.rs): `/api/mcp`, the room tools over MCP's Streamable HTTP transport ([ADR-0038](../../docs/adr/0038-rooms-and-guest-devices.md) decision 2, Y-534), and the owner's room routes: `GET /api/rooms`, `GET /api/rooms/{room}`, `POST /api/rooms/{room}/messages` (Y-536), `POST /api/rooms/{room}/resume`, and `POST /api/rooms`, `PATCH /api/rooms/{room}` and `DELETE /api/rooms/{room}` (Y-550). Every request passes `allowed()` first, so a non-owner is **403** and a `tailscale` that cannot answer is **503**; after that, a tool's failure is a result with `isError`. POST takes one JSON-RPC message and answers JSON: `initialize` echoes a revision from `room::PROTOCOL_VERSIONS`, `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`. A notification or a response is **202** with no body, a batch is **400**, and `GET` is **405**. `initialize` issues an `Mcp-Session-Id`; a call with no thread is that session's member, so two TUIs on one machine are two members. The label is the caller's machine, from `whois` joined to the tailnet list on the stable id, plus ` · chat <thread>` when `X-Yantra-Thread: <workspace>/<thread>` names a workspace on that machine: its ssh destination, without `user@`, is the node's name, DNS name, first label or address, or resolves to one through `ssh -G`. Any other header is ignored, and the body never sets it. `room_read`'s wait ends with an `isError` result when the daemon shuts down. `room_info` answers the room and each member with its presence as JSON text, and `room_status` takes one line of at most 120 characters and answers `{"ok":true}`; both refuse a room this daemon does not hold (Y-551). Resume answers **204**, or **404** for a room this daemon does not hold. A post takes `{text}`, labels it `owner on <machine>` from identity and never from the body, and answers `{seq, delivered}`; **404** is a room it does not hold and **400** an empty text or one over 16 KiB. The two `GET`s answer the summaries, and one room with its messages as `log` and its members as `presence`, or **404**. `GET /api/rooms/{room}/events?after=<seq>&wait=<s>` is the owner's long-poll (Y-551): it answers `{messages, presence, last}` at once when a message after `after` exists, and otherwise when one arrives, presence changes or `wait` runs out; `wait` above 50 is **400**, a room it does not hold **404**, and a daemon that shuts down **503**. A summary carries `workspace`, `brief` and `base`, and a message its `kind`. `POST /api/rooms` takes `{name, workspace, brief?, base?}` as application/json only and answers **201** with the summary; a bad field is **400**, a workspace that does not load **404**, an existing definition **409**. `PATCH` takes `{brief}`, `null` to clear, and an undefined room is **404**. `DELETE` answers `{"removed": bool}`.
- [src/room.rs](src/room.rs): the rooms in `Fleet::rooms`, a [`room::Rooms`](../yantra-core/src/room.rs) behind a mutex (Y-534). A send takes each member thread's unseen messages under the same lock, wraps them, and queues them for that thread; one task per thread sends them to `chat::wake` one wake at a time, so no request awaits ssh and a thread gets its messages in seq order. A wake resolves when a turn starts or cannot, a queued one included, and one that starts no turn gives the messages back to that thread. An ACP thread or a gone one is not woken again. `room_read` waits in memory on a `watch` that every message bumps, and counts as listening while it waits, however the wait ends. `events` waits on the same `watch`, on `chat::Registry::changed`, and until the next member turns away. A thread's presence comes from `chat::Registry::activity`. A room that pauses sends one ntfy notification that names the room and no text. `post` is the owner's message from the dashboard or `yantra room post`: it queues wakes the way a send does, for every member thread. `list` and `view` are the dashboard's reads. `create`, `edit` and `end` write `~/.config/yantra/rooms/<name>.toml` first and then change memory, under one lock (Y-550). A restart reloads each definition with one system message, skips a file that does not load, and loses every message, member, cursor, count and pause, and every room with no definition. The log names a room, a seq and counts, never a message's text (Q5).
- [src/carry.rs](src/carry.rs): `POST /api/carry` and `POST /api/carry/{id}` (Y-652), both behind `allowed()`. The first takes an object of strings, at most 1 MiB (**413** over it, **400** for any other shape), and answers `{id}`, 128 random bits in hex. The second answers that object and leaves it until it expires, because the old page has already removed its copy and a take whose answer is lost must be able to ask again; an expired or unknown id is a JSON **404**. The slots live in `Fleet`, at most 8 of 5 minutes, and a full store drops the oldest. Nothing goes to disk and no body is logged.
- [src/store.rs](src/store.rs): the thread store ([ADR-0045](../../docs/adr/0045-the-hub-keeps-a-thread-store.md), Y-688), `~/.local/state/yantra/threads.sqlite`, `0600` in a `0700` directory. One table, `threads`, keyed by workspace and id: the machine, branch, worktree, harness, session, a title cut at 80 characters, the status and three times. No message text and no secret. `rusqlite` with hand-written SQL; every connection sets `busy_timeout = 5000`, WAL and `synchronous = NORMAL`, and every call runs on `spawn_blocking` (I-12, I-13, I-14). Migrations run in order under `user_version`. The chat writes a session here before git config, and resumes the store's session when the two differ. The thread list adopts git config's rows once and never overwrites one. It marks a thread the machine no longer has `gone`; `DELETE …/threads/{thread}` forgets that row, which the dashboard's *Forget thread* and `yantra chat rm --daemon` send. It serves the rows as `offline` when ssh cannot reach the machine. `Store::search` backs **`GET /api/threads?q=`** (Y-689, in `write.rs`): a case-insensitive `LIKE` on titles with `%`, `_` and `\` escaped, newest activity first, at most 20, home rows skipped. A home thread's row has an empty workspace, branch and worktree, and `GET /api/machines/{machine}/threads` lists a machine's rows, home threads among them (ADR-0046, Y-699). The daemon refuses to start when the store does not open.
- [src/layout.rs](src/layout.rs): `GET` and `PUT /api/layout`, the dashboard layout in `~/.config/yantra/dashboard.json` ([ADR-0036](../../docs/adr/0036-the-dashboard-layout-syncs-through-the-daemon.md), Y-515), through [`yantra_core::layout`](../yantra-core/src/layout.rs). The `GET` is not gated and answers the default at `rev` 0 when there is no file. The `PUT` passes `allowed()` first, takes at most 64 KiB, and answers the saved layout; a stale `rev` is **409** with the current layout, a bad shape **400**, and a failed write **500**. A lock makes the read, the compare and the write one step. [tests/layout.rs](tests/layout.rs) proves the 409 and the atomic write in podman.
- [src/placement.rs](src/placement.rs): `POST /api/placement`, which machine a new session should open on (Y-517). The body is `{repo?: "owner/name", path?, folders?}`; neither field ranks on the heartbeat terms alone, and both is a **400**. It ranks the owner's machines with [placement.rs](../yantra-core/src/placement.rs) and answers `{ranked: [{machine, score, terms, reason, path?}], rejected: [{machine, why, age_seconds?}]}`. Which machines are asked over ssh, for how long, and how a workspace matches is core's `placement::ask`, which `yantra why --repo` calls too. A machine that does not answer is unknown and scores 0. "Where it ran" is a workspace in the read model on that machine that names the same repository or folder, because the daemon keeps no history of sessions. It is a read on the probe licence ([ADR-0019](../../docs/adr/0019-a-probe-that-asks-a-machine-is-a-post.md)), on `write.rs`'s authoriser. A daemon that has not looked at the tailnet is a **503**.
- [src/github.rs](src/github.rs): the grant in memory (Y-342, ADR-0023 §3) — token, login, scopes, whether a device flow is pending, and whether the last one ended on an expiring token — beside the beats rather than inside the snapshot, for the same reason they are. It is the `Forge` the attention sweep reads, so a sign-in changes the next reading rather than the next daemon, and it wakes the three GitHub classes when it changes. `sign_in` is the rest of the flow after the code was shown; the grant goes live whether or not the file could be written, and the journal says which.
- [src/terminal.rs](src/terminal.rs): `GET /api/workspaces/{name}/terminal` and `GET /api/machines/{machine}/sessions/{session}/terminal`, a WebSocket over [`yantra_core::pty`](../yantra-core/src/pty.rs). An upgrade is a `GET`, so it does **not** inherit `write.rs`'s check and calls `allowed()` by name — `up` starts a process Yantra chose, a terminal runs whatever is typed. Frames carry no envelope: binary is terminal bytes both ways, text is control — `{"rows":…,"cols":…,"term":…}` from the browser, required first because a pty opens with a window and a terminal (the `term` is the dashboard's own constant, never a user's — I-36), and a failure reason from the daemon, which a close frame cannot hold. **The stream is never logged** (Q5), and **never buffered**: a browser that lost its socket opens another, and the tmux on the far side draws the pane for whichever client attaches (Y-132). **Two addresses, one bridge** ([ADR-0022](../../docs/adr/0022-a-socket-may-address-a-session-rather-than-a-workspace.md)): a workspace is read for the machine and the session it names, so a caller holding both needs none — same `allowed()`, same protocol, same ping, and a session that is not there is refused by name. It holds ssh for as long as someone is looking, which the request path may not — and it does so after the upgrade has answered. **The daemon originates a ping every 20 s and ends the socket after two consecutive misses** (Y-134), which drops the `Terminal` and with it the `ssh`, the pty and the tmux client on the far side. A traffic timer would be wrong in both directions — output in progress is not idleness, silence is not death — and the pong is a protocol frame rather than the stream, so Q5 is untouched: a peer that answers is never closed however long it prints nothing. Since Y-394 a third route, `GET /api/machines/{machine}/install/{index}/terminal`, is [ADR-0030](../../docs/adr/0030-a-one-off-terminal-runs-only-a-command-an-install-left.md)'s one-off terminal: it runs the command at that place in what the latest install on the machine left (`Fleet::left`, in memory), never one the caller sends, and ends on an `{"exit": n}` text frame. Since Y-701 a fourth, `GET /api/machines/{machine}/owner/terminal?as=<admin>`, is [ADR-0046](../../docs/adr/0046-the-owner-types-sudo-in-an-owner-terminal.md) decision 2's owner terminal: `ssh -tt <admin>@<machine>` with no command and no tmux, the account's own login shell. It needs the owner's live session cookie (`write::signed_in_socket`: no cookie is 401, an agent token 403), refuses a bad machine or `as` with a `400` before the upgrade, and ends on `{"exit": n}` as the one-off does.
- [src/contract.rs](src/contract.rs): tests only. Renders every read route and every write DTO into [`web/src/contract.gen.ts`](../../web/src/contract.gen.ts), TypeScript that `satisfies` the dashboard's own types, and fails when the committed file no longer matches — `just fixtures` rewrites it. The seam between the daemon and the browser, checked rather than kept in step by convention (Y-124).
- [yantrad.service](yantrad.service): the systemd unit for the appliance (Y-142). `Restart=on-failure` with a `RestartSec` chosen against systemd's five-starts-in-ten-seconds limit, because `listen_on`'s refusal is the retry condition and a fast-exiting unit would otherwise sit in `failed` on a box with nobody at it; `After=tailscaled.service`, which orders the start and waits for no address. A **system** unit: a `--user` one cannot order against `tailscaled.service`, which the user manager does not have. [tests/service_unit.rs](tests/service_unit.rs) runs it under a real systemd in a disposable podman container, and `just appliance-install <host>` copies it onto a box beside the binary (Y-145) while [install.sh](../../install.sh) takes it out of the release archive `SHA256SUMS` covered (Y-365, [docs/appliance.md](../../docs/appliance.md)).
- [yantra-update.path](yantra-update.path) and [yantra-update.service](yantra-update.service): the update trigger and the root oneshot it starts (ADR-0027 §3, Y-368). The service removes the trigger, runs `/usr/local/bin/yantra-update` (the archive's own `install.sh`), and restarts `yantrad` and `yantra-agent` in `ExecStartPost=`, so a failed install restarts nothing. The request carries no version. Its `RuntimeDirectory` is `/run/yantra-update`, kept after a run, where `install.sh` writes its progress for `GET /api/about` (Y-612).
- [tests/installer.rs](tests/installer.rs): [install.sh](../../install.sh) run **twice** under the same real systemd, as an unprivileged account through `sudo` (Y-158). The second run is the row: an edited `/etc/yantra/agent.env` survives untouched (ADR-0013 §4) and all three binaries are replaced while one of them is executing — with `cp` measured refusing the same write, so the rename is evidence rather than ceremony (Y-145). github.com and api.github.com are [tests/fixture/release.sh](tests/fixture/release.sh) inside the container, which is what lets a **corrupted** archive, a release list that does not answer and an archive carrying no units all be served and refused. The fixture signs `SHA256SUMS` with its own key and writes that key into its copy of the script (Y-780, ADR-0027 decision 4): a release with no `SHA256SUMS.sig`, with another key's signature, or with a `SHA256SUMS` changed after the signature installs nothing, a signed one installs, and a script with no key says that it checked no signature. A run that does not name `--channel nightly` refuses a kept `nightly`, with or without the unit's `RUNTIME_DIRECTORY`. The cost is that the archive is the fixture's, so its shape is asserted against [release.yml](../../.github/workflows/release.yml). **No version appears in both this test and the script** (Y-365): the two the fixture publishes are its own, so the second run installing the newer one is the release being followed. No container holds a `tailscaled`, so the Tailscale step is proved by its report changing when a `tailscale` appears. The interactive runs (Y-384) go through a pty against a `tailscale` stub that logs its calls: a yes logs in, turns on `serve` and writes the box's own address into an absent `agent.env`, a second run asks nothing and changes no file, and a no installs Yantra and starts nothing. A rerun while both units run (Y-475) asks to restart them at a terminal: a no restarts nothing and prints the command, and a yes restarts both. With no terminal, with or without `--yes`, a rerun never asks, never restarts a running unit (ADR-0027 §5) and draws no QR code. A `qrencode` stub shows that a terminal run draws the URL as a QR code. A `--yes` run with no terminal (Y-474) logs in with `TS_AUTHKEY`, starts both units and ends on the dashboard's URL, and the key is in no file and no journal line afterwards; `YANTRA_YES=1` does the same on a second run, and an unknown flag is refused. A bare `debian:trixie` run (Y-473) proves a missing `curl` is installed with `apt-get`. `--agent` (Y-713) refuses where no `agent.env` is, and on a joined machine replaces the agent and its unit, keeps `agent.env`, restarts the agent, and writes no `yantrad`, `yantra`, daemon unit, `daemon.env`, channel file or `yantra` account.
- [src/dictate.rs](src/dictate.rs): `GET /api/dictate?workspace=<name>&thread=<id>`, the Chat's dictation ([ADR-0043](../../docs/adr/0043-dictation-runs-a-local-speech-model.md) §4, Y-682), a WebSocket behind `allowed()`, with the workspace name checked before the upgrade (**400**). Binary frames are 16 kHz mono s16le, held in RAM up to 60 seconds. The text frame `end` sends them to `$YANTRA_STT_URL/transcribe` with the hotwords from `yantra_core::stt`, which it starts building at the upgrade and waits for at most 5 s. One text frame answers: `{"text"}`, or `{"error", "said"}` and a close, where `error` is `off` (no URL), `unreachable`, `too-long`, `silent` (no audio, or no words) or `failed` (the service's status). It logs the lifecycle and the reason, and never a frame, a count, the text or a hotword; a TRACE test proves it. `main.rs`'s `unlogged` filter drops every `ureq`, `tungstenite` and `tokio_tungstenite` record whatever `RUST_LOG` says, because at TRACE they write each byte they carry; the TRACE test captures every thread and fails without it. `GET /api/dictate/health` answers `{state}`, `off`, `unreachable` or `ready`, from `$YANTRA_STT_URL/health` with a 2 s timeout: the HTTPS page cannot reach the service's address itself (§6).
- [src/mic.rs](src/mic.rs): `GET /api/machines/{machine}/mic`, the dashboard's push-to-talk ([ADR-0031](../../docs/adr/0031-the-microphone-reaches-a-machine-as-a-virtual-source.md) §5–6, Y-418), a WebSocket over [`yantra_core::mic`](../yantra-core/src/mic.rs). It calls `allowed()` before the upgrade and refuses a name outside the ssh-destination rule with a **400** (I-63). The upgrade starts `pw-cat` at once. Binary frames are 16 kHz mono s16le, copied to its stdin with no pty and no buffer; a text frame from the browser is ignored. The socket's close closes stdin, which ends `pw-cat`. A writer that could not start, stopped taking audio or exited sends one text frame with the reason, then a close. It reuses `terminal.rs`'s ping, so a vanished phone does not hold `pw-cat` open. **No audio byte and no byte count is logged** (Q5), and a test captures the log to prove it.
- [tests/mic.rs](tests/mic.rs): the virtual microphone set up for real (Y-417, [ADR-0031](../../docs/adr/0031-the-microphone-reaches-a-machine-as-a-virtual-source.md)) on the Fedora fixture's real systemd, sshd and user manager: Fedora's PipeWire packages through `sudo -n`, the drop-in, `yantra-mic` hearing a tone `pw-cat` plays into `yantra-mic-sink`, a default sink that is not `yantra-mic-sink`, the default source set only where the card list is empty, `doctor`'s `mic` check before and after, a second run that restarts nothing, and an account whose sudo asks leaving `sudo loginctl enable-linger` in the event's `commands`, which `doctor` then reads as an absent `mic` naming linger. A second test (Y-418) feeds `yantra_core::mic`'s writer a 440 Hz tone in 20 ms frames, records it from `yantra-mic`, and asserts that closing the stream leaves no `pw-cat` running.
- [tests/update.rs](tests/update.rs): the update end to end under a real systemd, sshd and tmux (Y-368). The real `yantrad` is published by the release fixture, a python client holds a terminal socket to a tmux session, and `POST /api/update` installs the next release. The session's processes survive, the socket reopens within `web/src/api/socket.ts`'s own `ATTEMPTS`×`PAUSE`, `yantrad.prev` is the old binary, and a corrupted archive restarts nothing. The real root unit refuses a nightly and a release with no `SHA256SUMS.sig`, and it replaces and restarts nothing (Y-780). A corrupted archive is also read back on `GET /api/about` as `failed`, in the unit's words (Y-612). A third test (Y-479) saves a client id over HTTP, asks for the same trigger, and finds the id in the restarted daemon's environment. [release.yml](../../.github/workflows/release.yml) also runs its last test on the x86_64 archive it built, which installs through its own `install.sh` and updates to a marked copy of itself, before anything is published (Y-483).
- [tests/own_box.rs](tests/own_box.rs): the box reached from itself (Y-598), under a real systemd, sshd, tmux, `yantrad` and `yantra`. `install.sh --yes` leaves a key and a `Host` block, and a session on the person's account appears in `GET /api/sessions` under the box's name. A second run adds neither again. The box's real `firstboot.sh` runs under its own unit (Y-786): `ssh -G` names `karigar`, that account is in no sudo group and `sudo -n` refuses it, and its session appears in the listing. Root with no account and a kept block for another account place no key and still finish, and the real update unit writes no file under either `.ssh`. It needs the workspace's `yantra` binary, so `-p yantrad` alone skips it. `tailscaled` is a stub and `/etc/hosts` stands in for MagicDNS.
- [tests/caddy_admin.rs](tests/caddy_admin.rs): Y-777's done test, under a real systemd and Fedora's Caddy. With the Caddyfile from before the row, `deploy` reads Caddy's config from `127.0.0.1:2019`. `install.sh`'s `close_the_admin_api` then adds `admin off` and restarts Caddy: the port refuses, the site still answers, and a second run changes nothing and restarts nothing. The global block [box/domain-setup.sh](../../box/domain-setup.sh) writes closes the port too. The function also closes the port where a comment or a CR follows the global block's brace and where a snippet stands before the block. Where `caddy adapt` refuses the file with the line added, the Caddyfile and the running Caddy stay as they were.
- [tests/rooms.rs](tests/rooms.rs): Y-534's done test, on `chat_keeper.rs`'s scaffolding and lock. A real `yantrad` reaches two podman fixtures, `alpha` and `beta`; the `tailscale` shim answers `whois` per address, and the test connects from 127.0.0.2, 127.0.0.3 or 127.0.0.4 to play each machine. Workspace `wa` names alpha as `yantra@alpha.example.ts.net`, not by its Tailscale name. It proves each turn's `--mcp-config`, a message from thread A waking thread B in `acceptEdits`, B's reply waking A without A's own message, a waiting `room_read`, the pause at 20 and the resume, and a 403 for another user. The Claude stand-in records its arguments; no real `claude` calls the route.
- [tests/secrets.rs](tests/secrets.rs): Y-647's done test, with no podman. A real `yantrad` starts with `YANTRA_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `YANTRA_NTFY_TOKEN` and `YANTRA_NTFY_URL` set, and its `ssh` and `tailscale` are shims that write their environment to a file. After the first refresh and a terminal socket, no recorded environment names any of `yantra_core::SECRETS`, and each holds `PATH`. It takes `chat_keeper.rs`'s lock, because the daemon binds 7717.
- [src/heartbeat.rs](src/heartbeat.rs): `POST /heartbeat`, the write `yantra-agent` makes. 204 with an empty body, a 4 KB limit, strict parsing, and identity taken from the source address rather than the payload. Holds `Beats`, one in-memory row per machine keyed on the node id, overwritten every beat.

## What decides its shape

- [ADR-0005](../../docs/adr/0005-core-logic-in-a-library-crate.md): the logic lives in the library; this crate stays thin.
- [ADR-0013](../../docs/adr/0013-the-heartbeat-carries-only-what-placement-scores.md): what `POST /heartbeat` accepts, why it answers nothing, and why the source address is the identity.
- [ADR-0004](../../docs/adr/0004-rust-for-the-daemon.md): Rust, with axum and tokio. TypeScript belongs to the browser — do not introduce a second runtime here.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): what is already settled, and what to read before starting — including why there is no `--bind` flag.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): a symlink to CLAUDE.md, for agents that read AGENTS.md.

## Optional

- [tracker.md](tracker.md): the invariants for the daemon: SQLite's I-12, I-13 and I-14, which [src/store.rs](src/store.rs) follows, and scheduling and PTY ones no shipped code exercises yet, plus the ones read off the daemon that does: I-58, `listen_on` runs once, so an address that moves under a healthy process is never noticed and `Restart=on-failure` never fires; I-59, the same supervisor re-arming *the first look says nothing* and swallowing every change a restart straddles; I-60, a startup check over something the filesystem owns being no guarantee at request time, enforced in [src/web.rs](src/web.rs); I-63, a machine name reaching `ssh`'s argv from a URL with nothing between it and the process, which ADR-0009 makes unavoidable and Y-329 closed with `--` before the destination in [yantra-core/src/ssh.rs](../yantra-core/src/ssh.rs); and I-64, a nested router with no fallback of its own handing a miss to the outer one — the dashboard — so an absent `/api` route answered `200 text/html`, enforced in [src/api.rs](src/api.rs). **I-60, I-63 and I-64 are the three that shipped code enforces rather than merely records; I-60 and I-64 are the two anyone has seen.**
- [../../tracker.md](../../tracker.md): M4 is the milestone that needs this. Open decisions that affect it are listed there.
- [docs/vision.md](../../docs/vision.md): what the daemon is ultimately for.
